title: American craft styles
lead: From cream ale to imperial stout, barrels and fruit: the styles American brewers made their own.

sections.name: Easy ales

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Cream ale, blonde and American wheat.

know: Cream ale: pale, crisp ale made to rival lager.
Blonde: a brewery’s easy house ale.
American wheat: bready, no banana or clove (Bell’s Oberon).

sections.name: IPAs: West Coast, hazy, double
know: West Coast: clear, dry, sharply bitter.
Double IPA: 7.5–10%, intensely hoppy but dry.

sections.name: Stouts and barleywine
know: American stout: roasty with American hops.
Imperial stout: 8–12%, once shipped to Russia’s court.
American barleywine: much hoppier than English.

sections.name: Barrels, fruit and spice
know: Barrel-aged: spirits barrels add their character.
Fruit and spice should taste real and balanced.
Pastry stouts and fruited sours are newer.
sections.source: BJCP 2021 Style Guidelines, 29A, 30A, 33A, 33B (bjcp.org); Cicerone, US Certified Cicerone Syllabus v6.0 (cicerone.org)

read.where: **Cream ale** (4.2–5.6%) is a very pale, crisp, fizzy **ale** first brewed in the 1800s to compete with lager; Genesee is the classic. **Blonde ale** (3.8–5.5%) is easy and clean, often a brewery’s **entry-level** house beer. **American wheat** (4–5.5%) is bready with **clean** yeast, so **no banana or clove**: Anchor made the first in 1984, and Michigan’s **Bell’s Oberon** is a listed example.
read.mixup: American wheat and Hefeweizen look alike. The Hefeweizen has banana and clove; the American one doesn’t.
read.sayIt: If you like light lagers, try the blonde. It’s easy and clean.

read.where: **West Coast IPA** is BJCP’s American IPA at its driest: **clear**, sharply **bitter**, 5.5–7.5%. **Hazy IPA** is **soft** and **juicy** with lower perceived bitterness; the haze should come from hops and grain proteins, not floating yeast. **Double IPA** (7.5–10%, 60–100 IBU) is intensely hoppy and bitter but stays **dry** and drinkable, without barleywine’s sweetness; Russian River **Pliny the Elder** (2000) made it famous.
read.mixup: Double IPA isn’t sweet. If it tastes rich and malty, that’s closer to barleywine.
read.sayIt: Do you like it bitter and crisp, or soft and juicy? That decides which IPA.

read.where: **American stout** (5–7%) is black, strongly **roasted** and bitter, with American hops: Michigan’s **Bell’s Kalamazoo Stout** is an example. **Imperial stout** (8–12%) traces to strong English porters exported in the 1700s, said to be popular at the **Russian imperial court**; it has roast, **dark fruit** and a warming finish (Old Rasputin, Bell’s Expedition). **American barleywine** (8–12%) is much **hoppier** than the English kind; Sierra Nevada Bigfoot (1983) set the standard.
read.mixup: “Imperial” on any style just means a stronger version.
read.sayIt: It’s an imperial stout, about 10%: chocolate, coffee, dark fruit. Best sipped.

keyPoints.line: the barrel’s old spirit adds flavor.

read.where: **Wood-aged** beer rests on oak; **barrel-aged** beer sits in barrels that held **spirits** like bourbon, whose character adds to the beer. They’re usually stronger and darker than the base style. **Fruit** and **spice** beers should taste of the real ingredient, in **balance**, and still taste like beer: Founders Breakfast Stout and Bell’s Cherry Stout are listed examples. Cicerone also expects you to know newer styles by producer: **pastry stouts** and **fruited sours**.
read.mixup: Barrel-aged doesn’t mean sour. A bourbon-barrel stout is rich and boozy, not tart.
read.sayIt: It spent time in bourbon barrels, so expect vanilla and a little whiskey warmth.

sources: BJCP 2021 Style Guidelines, 1C, 1D, 18A, 20B, 20C, 21A, 21C, 22A, 22C, 29A, 30A, 33A, 33B (bjcp.org); Cicerone, US Certified Cicerone Syllabus v6.0 (cicerone.org). Checked Nov 8, 2026.

cards.answer: A pale, crisp ale made to rival lager

cards.q: American wheat beer differs from Hefeweizen because…
cards.answer: It has no banana or clove

cards.q: What should a double IPA not be?
Imperial stout is linked in history to…

cards.answer: Character from the barrel’s old spirit
Tastes of real fruit, in balance, and still like beer

unverified: ABV and IBU ranges are guideline ranges; brands vary.
